correction_history: Before any learning result, an internal verification caught that the first draft of this amendment compared a distance using drive weights normalized to sum one with an output energy using unnormalized relative variances. All relative-error values and threshold crossings below use one consistent normalization.
unchanged_parts: registered low-band and high-band distance crossover
reason_for_amendment: The original target-example budgets 1, 2, 4, and 8 do not span the registered 1% aggregate relative-RMS threshold under the exact minimum-change adaptation null. The phrase 'band-resolved 1% relative RMS' also left its normalization implicit.

analytic_null.description: Adapt the exact source response operator by the smallest Hilbert-Schmidt-norm change that interpolates n noiseless target excitations.
assumptions: The 16 boundary coefficients are whitened to an isotropic drive vector z.
Source and target response operators B_S and B_T map z to the observed field.
The n target drive vectors are independent and isotropic.
The adapted operator exactly interpolates the n target observations.
analytic_null.solution: B_hat = B_S + (B_T-B_S) P_Z, where P_Z projects onto the span of the n target drive vectors.
analytic_null.bandwise_extension: The same factor multiplies the squared error after projection onto either orthogonal output-mode band.

aggregate.prediction: P and G tie at every target-data budget because their total squared response distances are matched.

bandwise.prediction: P has lower expected error in modes 1-8 and G has lower expected error in modes 17-24 at every nonterminal budget.

registered_rivals_after_amendment.minimum_change_response_reuse: Aggregate P/G tie plus the preregistered opposite band winners, with the exact 1-n/16 retention law.
registered_rivals_after_amendment.categorical_physical_regime_reuse: P has lower error than G in both bands, overturning the null's high-band winner.
registered_rivals_after_amendment.categorical_geometry_scaffold_reuse: G has lower error than P in both bands, overturning the null's low-band winner.
registered_rivals_after_amendment.representation_dependent_transfer: Departures from the null change sign across prospectively declared learner classes.
registered_rivals_after_amendment.no_useful_transfer: Source initialization does not improve on an equally capable target-only learner.

amended_outcomes.primary: Band-resolved error curves relative to the exact minimum-change null, rather than a threshold crossing alone.
amended_outcomes.threshold_reporting: Report aggregate-relative and per-band-relative normalization separately.
amended_outcomes.architecture_language: Call a pattern architecture-robust only over prospectively declared learner classes; do not call it architecture-independent.

interpretation_limits: The null assumes exact source operators, noiseless labels, isotropic whitened drives, and minimum-Hilbert-Schmidt-change interpolation.
It is a mechanistic reference, not a claim that neural fine-tuning obeys this rule.
A practical learner can differ because of representation, optimization, finite source error, regularization, or coupling among modes.
No learning result was inspected before deriving or recording this amendment.
